findings.desc: done_closure now classifies done-required-validation as a done_prepare recovery blocker and returns only lattice done_prepare as the nextCommand, but done_prepare never invokes the separate done_required_validate writer. Its validate step calls ordinary lattice validate, then rebuilds done_closure; missing or stale done-required-evidence.json is produced only by done_required_validate. For opted-in doneRequiredCommands this routes the operator into a loop instead of creating post-merge material/storyFilesHash-bound DONE-required evidence, so the ordering-sensitive blocker is not actually recovered by the host-neutral command.

Test coverage does not prove the new done_prepare recovery path actually resolves missing DONE-required evidence. The new smoke scenario only builds the DONE checklist/runbook and asserts branch-synced-main plus done-required-validation nextCommand values point at lattice done_prepare; it never executes done_prepare for that missing evidence case. Existing DONE-required smoke pre-runs done_required_validate before done_prepare, so it only covers already-present evidence. Meanwhile done_closure maps done-required-validation to done_prepare, but done_prepare only runs ordinary lattice validate before rebuilding done_closure and does not invoke done_required_validate. A missing DONE-required blocker can therefore be routed to a command that rechecks and blocks again, and the current regression coverage would not catch the stale/DONE recovery loop.
